taxonomy.note: This record uses D. carnegii, known from the nearly complete holotype CM 84. The original type species, D. longus, is based on scrappy tail bones and was judged a nomen dubium by Tschopp et al. (2015), who proposed that the ICZN make D. carnegii the type species.

timeRange.note: Stage-level PBDB occurrence ages for D. carnegii in the Morrison Formation (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian).

massKg.note: Museum figure for the genus; no species-level peer-reviewed estimate was verified.

text.en: Diplodocus was one of the longest dinosaurs, a plant-eater from the Late Jurassic of western North America, about 150 million years ago. Its very long, whip-like tail made up much of that length. It used its long neck to reach plants at different heights and to drink. Its name, 'double beam', refers to the two-pronged bones under its tail. All known fossils come from the Morrison Formation in the USA.
'Dippy', the Natural History Museum's famous Diplodocus cast, was a gift from Andrew Carnegie in 1905.
